correctness.rationale: The support-functional criterion exhausts Birkhoff pairs on a polygon: an interior facet point has a unique norming facet and hence a unique kernel direction, while at a vertex the convex segment of adjacent norming facets sweeps one opposite-perpendicular facet. For the regular decagon this reduces, after dihedral symmetry and swapping the symmetric objective, to x=(1,t), |t|<=tan(pi/10), and y=(0,sec(pi/10)). The directions of x+y and x-y stay in the two claimed normal sectors, so their norms are affine in t. Their squared difference simplifies to a positive multiple of t, forcing the maximum to the vertex endpoint. Exact substitution gives ||x+y||=(1+sqrt(5))/2 and ||x-y||=sqrt(5)-1, hence C_B=(5sqrt(5)-9)/8.
risks: The reduction uses the support-functional characterization of Birkhoff orthogonality; it is stated explicitly and the polygonal incidence is checked in the bundled script.
The exact theorem is for the decagon only; no extrapolation to all regular Radon polygons is used.

value.rationale: C_B was introduced specifically to quantify the gap between Birkhoff and isosceles orthogonality and to measure a cosine in Birkhoff-right triangles. The defining paper identifies only the Radon extremizer, the affine-regular hexagon. The affine-regular decagon is the next canonical regular Radon polygon, so its exact nonextremal value gives a natural benchmark showing how far the new invariant has already moved toward the Hilbert value 0. The proof is not merely a table lookup: it identifies the complete Birkhoff incidence reduction and turns the continuous optimization into a sharp one-parameter affine law.
risks: The contribution is a canonical exact benchmark rather than a classification of all regular Radon polygons.
